key_insight: Adding mean-flow skew to a turbulent mixing layer changes the magnitudes of mean and turbulent statistics by up to about 40%, but the flow still follows the same core similarity and growth behavior.
engineering_relevance: This provides an experimental benchmark for predicting and controlling 3D free-shear flows in practical systems where streams meet at non-parallel angles.
method: Introduced spanwise flow skew using turning vanes near the splitter-plate trailing edge.
Measured downstream velocity statistics with cross-wire anemometry.
Compared planar and skewed mixing layers using similarity scaling and Reynolds-stress profiles.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports systematic reductions in mean and turbulent quantities of roughly 40% in the skewed case, while similarity collapse, linear shear-layer growth, and near-Gaussian stress profiles were retained.
watch_item: The results are experimentally specific, so different skew geometries or Reynolds numbers may alter the quantitative shifts even if the qualitative trends remain.
paper_title: Effects of mean flow skew on turbulent shear layers. Part II. Experimental investigation
